purpose: prospectively re-bind the Phase-25A trainer after an execution-mechanism-only hardening, and record the teardown incident

changes: checkpoint writes are atomic (temp file + os.replace)
history.csv and config.json / run.json writes are atomic
history row is persisted BEFORE the checkpoint, so a checkpoint always carries history for epochs 0..epoch (contiguous on resume)
resume restores ALL RNG state (python / numpy / torch CPU / torch CUDA) with CPU-uint8 coercion; previously the RNG was NOT restored
resume refuses to continue when a checkpoint lacks RNG state
resume falls back to best.pt when latest.pt is unreadable
idempotency guard: --resume on a completed run is a no-op
rebind_history.supersedes_note: the pre-hardening trainer SHA was not recorded in any run artefact; it is identified by the artefacts it produced, preserved in the quarantine directory

incident.cause: external process-tree teardown by the execution harness (clean log, no traceback, no crash event)
incident.note: the defect corrupted OUTPUT ARTEFACTS, not computed results; no epoch produced a wrong number

disposition.action: RESTART fold0 FROM EPOCH 0 under the hardened trainer
disposition.rationale: best.pt was written under the pre-hardening trainer whose history was persisted AFTER the checkpoint, so its history covers epochs 0..24 while its weights are epoch 25. Resuming from it would leave a one-epoch gap in the history. Restarting under ONE trainer SHA yields a contiguous, self-consistent run. The cost is ~18 minutes.
disposition.alternative_rejected: resume from best.pt with start_epoch=26 (history gap) or start_epoch=25 (epoch replay from post-epoch weights, not bit-exact)
disposition.equivalence_evidence: the restarted run must reproduce the per-epoch metrics logged for epochs 0..29 of the interrupted run, which is direct evidence that restart-from-0 is scientifically equivalent to an uninterrupted run
